subject: Clarifying timelines, hosting & SLA targets for Medicore evaluation
messages:
From: Alex Torres <atorres@medicore.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandeep Rao <sandeep.rao@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Redwood fit for patient-eligibility feature

Thanks again for the demo this morning — appreciate the walkthrough. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can align procurement + security paths.

Summary of what we discussed:
- Use case: real-time patient eligibility checks inside our clinical workflow tool (avg request ~120 tokens, some spike paths up to 400 tokens).
- Priority: low latency on the critical path (triage screen) + predictable unit economics for 10–20M tokens/month if we roll to prod.
- Initial proposal: hosted API for PoC, reserved capacity (dedicated) for production, optional private deployment if legal requires on-prem.

Stakeholders (on our side):
- Econ buyer: Lina Park, CFO (decision on spend)
- Security lead: Sandeep Rao (I copied him) — will lead the RFI / SOC2 review
- Procurement: Priya Menon — will handle contract/redlines and standard SLA asks

Questions we need answered to get internal alignment:
1) Target latency envelope: can you confirm p95 targets for 128–256 token requests on Hosted vs Dedicated? We need numbers to lock the UX bar.
2) Cost guidance: rough unit cost for hosted baseline and a ballpark for dedicated reserved pricing at our target volume (10–20M tokens/month).
3) SLA: what uptime and support response windows do you offer at enterprise tier? Are there playbooks for failover (region/model fallback)?
4) RFI / evidence: can you share SOC2 artifacts and a short SLO/SLA draft we can hand to procurement?

Next steps from our side: Sandeep will send a short RFI this week, Priya will coordinate procurement timeline once we have numbers. Lina wants a rough timeline to present to execs (are we talking 6–8 weeks to contract after procurement kickoff?).

Attaching the RFI template we use for vendors (I will send the official doc in a follow-up).

Thanks —Alex

[Attachment stub: Medicore_RFI.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@medicore.com>
Cc: Sandeep Rao <sandeep.rao@medicore.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Redwood fit for patient-eligibility feature

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and for outlining the internal owners. Quick answers and proposed next steps below; copying Ben (pricing/solutions) and Marissa (AE lead) to keep alignment.

TL;DR answers:
- Latency (p95): Hosted API: ~80–130 ms p95 for 128-token requests; ~120–220 ms p95 for 256-token requests, depending on model family and region. Dedicated (reserved) pools: ~35–80 ms p95 for 128 tokens, ~60–140 ms p95 for 256 tokens. Those are measured on our benchmark workloads — we’ll model specifics to your token mix.
- Cost (ballpark): Hosted: $0.30–0.60 per 1k tokens (model-dependent). Dedicated reserved pricing materially lowers unit cost at 10–20M tokens/month; typical committed discounts reduce unit cost by ~40–60% versus hosted (we'll run a tailored quote).
- SLA / support: Enterprise SLA offers 99.9% uptime target, incident response 1 hour for Sev 1, 4 hours for Sev 2 during business hours; 24/7 response can be included for an enterprise support add-on. We provide automated model fallback and region failover policies in the console; playbooks exist and we'll attach an SLO draft.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II summary + controls map available; we can provide an encrypted bundle to Sandeep under an NDA. Also attaching a short SLO draft and our standard SOW template.

Questions we have for you (so Ben can model pricing and infra):
- Can you confirm expected p95 token length distribution (percent of requests <=128, 129–256, >256)? Even a rough split (e.g., 70/20/10) will help.
- Are there hard requirements for data residency / VPC (e.g., must stay in a specific cloud region or on-prem)?
- Procurement timeline: what does success look like for Lina — preferred contract length, & any internal procurement windows we should know about?

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben will produce a 1-page pricing delta between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with assumptions by Thu (Sep 2).
2) I’ll share SOC2 summary + SLO draft under CDA by EOD tomorrow.
3) Schedule a 30-min procurement + security sync (Priya + Sandeep + our legal), propose Wed Sep 1 or Fri Sep 3.

If that aligns, Ben — please prepare assumptions and a simple cost model. Marissa — I’ll sync with you on timing for exec-facing summary.

Best,
Kimberly
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

[Attachment stub: Redwood_SLO-draft.docx]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <atorres@medicore.com>, Sandeep Rao <sandeep.rao@medicore.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Redwood fit for patient-eligibility feature — initial cost assumptions

Hi team — putting initial assumptions and a simple line-item model below so Medicore has something to review in the sync. I will formalize into a one-pager by Thu.

Assumptions used (please confirm):
- Monthly token volume: 15M tokens (mid of 10–20M).
- Mix: 65% <=128 tokens, 25% 129–256, 10% >256.
- Model family: mid-sized performant open model (we used schema similar to rw-mid-3b in our bench).

Quick cost delta (ballpark):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): ~ $0.45 / 1k tokens => ~ $6,750 / month at 15M tokens.
- Dedicated (reserved): committed 12-mo: effective ~ $0.20 / 1k tokens => ~ $3,000 / month (includes reserved GPU pools + support).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): up-front onboarding + infra op costs; unit economics can be similar to dedicated but requires procurement of infra and a longer lead time (6–12 weeks to deploy).

Latency guidance we will model against your token mix; the numbers Kimberly shared are our bench baselines. For procurement talking points: dedicated gives you the best predictable throughput and p95 SLAs; hosted is fastest to start for a PoC.

Deliverables for Thu (Sep 2):
- One-page hosted vs dedicated vs private cost comparison (assumptions clearly called out).
- Short FAQ for procurement: termination terms, data retention, audit rights, sample SLA terms.

If Alex / Sandeep can confirm the token mix and any residency constraints today, I’ll finalize.

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer

[Attachment stub: Redwood_SOW-template.docx]

From: Alex Torres <atorres@medicore.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandeep Rao <sandeep.rao@medicore.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@medicore.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, legal@medicore.com
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Redwood fit for patient-eligibility feature — procurement sync request

Thanks — that looks good and very actionable. Quick replies inline: 
- Token mix: we ran a small sample and the distribution Ben used (65/25/10) is a close match — confirm.
- Residency: must remain within us regions (no EU data movement) — VPC / dedicated in us-east or us-west preferred.
- Timeline: Lina is comfortable with a 60-day procurement window once we have pricing and an SLO to review; she wants the exec summary by Sep 10.

Sandeep will send the RFI with a couple technical questions today. Priya will join the procurement sync — Wed Sep 1 10:00 AM PT works for us (please send calendar invite).

Also: Can you include a short paragraph we can give our legal on how Redwood handles model fallback and graceful degradation (we want simple language for contract).

Appreciate it — Alex
